question.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the numerator using $1-{cos}^{2}⁡x={sin}^{2}⁡x.$

$$
\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x-1}=\frac{1-{cos}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x-1}
$$

Next, we factor the numerator as a difference of squares, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1-{cos}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x-1} & =\frac{(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x-1} \\  & =-\frac{(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x} \\  & =-\frac{(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\cancel{(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}}{\cancel{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x}} \\  & =-\frac{1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{1} \\  & =-(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that:

$$
\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡x}{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x}=-(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)
$$
